entries.appliesTo: controllers and processors of agricultural data collected, produced, or generated in Nebraska

dutySources.consent-workflow: Sec. 5(1) — 'A controller or processor shall not engage in the sale of agricultural data without the express written consent of the agricultural producer.'
dutySources.risk-program: Sec. 7(1) — 'Any controller or processor in custody or possession of agricultural data shall establish, implement, and maintain reasonable administrative, technical, and physical data security practices to protect the confidentiality, integrity, and accessibility of such agricultural data.'

exposure.enforcer: attorney-general (exclusive remedy, no private cause of action)

sources.appliesTo: Sec. 3(3)(a) — 'collected, produced, or generated in this state and is linked or reasonably linked to an identified or reasonably identifiable agricultural producer'
sources.penaltyMax: Sec. 8(1)(b) — 'Recover a civil penalty in the amount of one thousand dollars for each separate violation.'
sources.penaltyUnit: Sec. 8(1)(b) — 'one thousand dollars for each separate violation'
sources.enforcer: Sec. 8(1) — 'The Attorney General may bring an action in the district court of Lancaster County against any controller or processor that violates the Agricultural Data Privacy Act'; Sec. 8(2) — 'shall not be construed to create any new private cause of action. The enforcement authority granted to the Attorney General under this section shall be the exclusive remedy for violations of the Agricultural Data Privacy Act.'
sources.cureDays: Sec. 9(2) — 'No such action for a civil penalty shall be initiated if, within forty-five days after receiving the written notice, the controller or processor: (a) Cures each such alleged violation'

flags: segment contains no AI-specific provisions — it is a general agricultural data privacy act; privacy-data is the nearest family but none of its fixed params (admOptOut, profilingAssessment, minorsFocus, registration) are set by the text

consent-workflow here is consent for data SALE, not likeness/replica use: Sec. 5(2) requires consent 'through a clear and conspicuous disclosure that is separate from the primary terms of service or data use agreement'
risk-program coded for Sec. 7 data-security practices, not an AI governance program

Sec. 6(1): beginning January 1, 2027, 'every new contract or agreement involving the collection or processing of agricultural data in this state shall contain a specific provision' prohibiting sale without consent — mandatory contract clause fits no listed duty key
Sec. 6(2): contract waivers of the act are 'void and unenforceable'
45-day cure right (Sec. 9) applies only to violations of secs. 6 and 7; Sec. 9(3): 'This section shall not apply to any violation of section 5 of this act' (the sale-consent requirement)
Sec. 4(2) declares the agricultural producer 'is the owner, and has control, of' originating data — ownership/property provision, not a duty

Sec. 11 amends public-records statute 84-712.05 to exempt agricultural data from disclosure 'unless prior written consent has been obtained from the owner of such agricultural data' (84-712.05(30)) — binds public custodians, noted here per category rule

entries.appliesTo: operators of conversational artificial intelligence services accessible to the general public

dutySources.disclosure-ui: Sec. 14(1) — 'An operator shall clearly and conspicuously disclose to each minor account holder that such minor account holder is interacting with artificial intelligence'; Sec. 15 — 'If a reasonable person interacting with a conversational artificial intelligence service would be misled to believe that the person is interacting with a human, an operator shall clearly and conspicuously disclose that the conversational artificial intelligence service is artificial intelligence.'
dutySources.content-safeguards: Sec. 14(3) — 'An operator shall, for minor account holders, institute reasonable measures to prevent the conversational artificial intelligence service from: (a) Producing visual depictions of sexually explicit conduct'; Sec. 14(4) — 'institute reasonable measures to prevent the conversational artificial intelligence service from generating statements that would lead a reasonable person to believe that they are interacting with a human'
dutySources.crisis-protocol: Sec. 16 — 'An operator shall adopt a protocol for the conversational artificial intelligence service to respond to user prompts regarding suicidal ideation or self-harm that includes, but is not limited to, making reasonable efforts to provide a response to the user that refers them to crisis service providers'

sources.scope: Sec. 13(2)(a) — 'an artificial intelligence software application, web interface, or computer program that is accessible to the general public and that primarily simulates human conversation and interaction through textual, visual, or aural communications'
sources.ageFocus: Sec. 14(1) — 'disclose to each minor account holder'; Sec. 14(3) — 'shall, for minor account holders, institute reasonable measures'
sources.aiDisclosure: Sec. 14(1) — '(a) As a persistent visible disclaimer; or (b) Both: (i) At the beginning of each session; and (ii) Appearing at least every three hours in a continuous conversational artificial intelligence service interaction.'
sources.crisisProtocol: Sec. 16 — 'shall adopt a protocol for the conversational artificial intelligence service to respond to user prompts regarding suicidal ideation or self-harm'
sources.engagementLimits: Sec. 14(2) — 'An operator shall not provide a minor account holder with points or similar rewards at unpredictable intervals with the intent to encourage increased engagement with the conversational artificial intelligence service.'
sources.parentalTools: Sec. 14(5) — 'An operator shall offer tools for minor account holders, and, when such account holders are younger than thirteen years of age, their parents or guardians, to manage the account holders' privacy and account settings.'
sources.contentSafeguards: Sec. 14(3) — 'institute reasonable measures to prevent the conversational artificial intelligence service from: (a) Producing visual depictions of sexually explicit conduct'
sources.ageThreshold: Sec. 13(4) — 'Minor means an individual that, based upon the circumstance, the operator has actual knowledge or reasonable certainty is younger than eighteen years of age'
sources.penaltyMax: Sec. 18(2)(b)(iii) — 'Civil penalties of at least one thousand dollars per violation, but in no event more than five hundred thousand dollars per operator.'
sources.penaltyUnit: Sec. 18(2)(b)(iii) — 'in no event more than five hundred thousand dollars per operator'
sources.enforcer: Sec. 18(1) — 'The Attorney General may enforce the Conversational Artificial Intelligence Safety Act.'; Sec. 18(3) — 'Nothing in the Conversational Artificial Intelligence Safety Act shall be interpreted as creating a private right of action.'

flags: statutory-review carried by the agricultural-data-privacy segment (omnibus rule 9)

scope enum lossy: Sec. 13(2)(b) excludes developer/researcher tools, embedded features, narrow-and-discrete-topic outputs, services 'primarily designed and marketed for commercial use by business entities', device voice assistants, internal business use, and customer-service-only uses
ageFocus lossy: Sec. 14 duties bind only as to minor account holders, but Sec. 15 (misled-reasonable-person disclosure), Sec. 16 (crisis protocol), and Sec. 17 apply to all users

aiDisclosure lossy: Sec. 14(1) permits either 'a persistent visible disclaimer' or session-start plus every-three-hours disclosure; coded periodic as the closest single enum because compliance path (b) requires BOTH session-start and recurring three-hour disclosure, and path (a) is continuous

content-safeguards includes anti-anthropomorphism measures: sentience/human claims, simulated emotional dependence, romantic or sexual innuendos, and 'Role-playing of adult-minor romantic relationships' (Sec. 14(4))

secondary age threshold: parental/guardian tools mandatory when account holders are 'younger than thirteen years of age'; for 13 and older, tools offered 'as appropriate based on relevant risks' (Sec. 14(5))

Sec. 17 prohibits operators from knowingly programming the service to state it 'is designed to provide professional mental or behavioral health care' — conduct prohibition adjacent to content-safeguards, fits no listed duty key

penalty structure: floor of 'at least one thousand dollars per violation' with $500,000 aggregate cap per operator; AG may also recover actual damages, court costs, attorney's fees, investigative costs (Sec. 18(2)(b))
AG may sue 'on behalf of the State of Nebraska or on behalf of any person aggrieved' (Sec. 18(2)(a))
developer liability shield: no liability for 'the developer of an artificial intelligence model' for violations by a third-party operator's system (Sec. 18(4))
